contracts.commit_point: The blocking dict returned inside the fetch_web_page branch of validate_tool_call (app/safety.py:143-147, 153-158, 160-167) at ADK tool dispatch — before the tool function executes at app/agent.py:59 and therefore before the underlying HTTP request is issued.
contracts.declared_mechanism: before_tool_callback=domain_safety_guard on scout_agent (app/agent.py:111); validate_tool_call's fetch_web_page branch (app/safety.py:135-167) performs scheme, netloc-keyword, and TLD checks against app/policies.yaml security lists loaded by PolicyService (app/safety.py:24-38).
contracts.forbidden_condition: fetch_web_page invoked with (a) a URL whose parsed scheme is not http or https (app/safety.py:142-147), (b) a netloc containing any security.blocked_keywords entry such as facebook.com, twitter.com, reddit.com (app/safety.py:151-158; app/policies.yaml:31-41), or (c) a netloc ending with any security.blocked_tlds entry such as .xyz or .tk (app/safety.py:160-167; app/policies.yaml:42-52); a missing URL argument also errors out (app/safety.py:136-138).
pending_binding_information: app/mcp_server.py is not among the supplied sources; the concrete HTTP request site for fetch_web_page (invoked at app/agent.py:59 via mcp_fetch_web_page) cannot be line-cited, so the exact commit of the network effect is bound only at guard interception rather than at the request issuance point.
contracts.protected_operation: Outbound web-page fetch performed by the fetch_web_page tool (wrapper at app/agent.py:53-59 delegating to mcp_fetch_web_page), registered on and instructed for scout_agent.
contracts.protected_resource: External web pages reachable via caller-supplied URL and retrieved by the tool's underlying HTTP client.
contracts.protection_obligation: Every fetch_web_page invocation must pass domain_safety_guard's URL structural checks before the page fetch executes: the URL argument must be present, must use scheme http or https, must not contain any blacklisted social-domain keyword in the host, and must not end with any blacklisted TLD (per app/policies.yaml security lists); violating calls are denied pre-execution.
scope_limits: URL checks trigger only when tool.name == 'fetch_web_page' (app/safety.py:135); other potentially network-bound tools (e.g., search_competitor_pricing_news) receive no scheme/domain/TLD screening from this guard.

Domain matching is substring containment in the lowercased netloc and TLD matching is suffix endswith, exactly as coded (app/safety.py:149-167); bypass tolerance (e.g., lookalike domains, userinfo tricks) is not assessed here.

The URL checks bind only agent-mediated tool dispatch; any direct call path to mcp_fetch_web_page (imported at app/agent.py:45) outside agent tool execution would not be guarded, and no such path is shown in supplied source.

contracts.commit_point: The blocking dict returned by PolicyService.validate_tool_call for an unauthorized pair (app/safety.py:122-127); per the declared callback contract (app/safety.py:117-119: dict = safety block, None = allow), the denial commits at this pre-execution return, before the invoked tool body runs and before any downstream effect.
contracts.declared_mechanism: before_tool_callback=domain_safety_guard registered on each Agent (app/agent.py:111, 129, 144, 180); domain_safety_guard delegates to policy_service.validate_tool_call (app/safety.py:174-176), whose is_tool_allowed check (app/safety.py:40-55) returns a blocking dict for tool names outside the role's allowed_tools loaded from app/policies.yaml (app/safety.py:24-38, app/policies.yaml:7-28).
contracts.forbidden_condition: A tool invocation proceeding to execution where the invoking agent's name (tool_context.agent_name) paired with tool.name is not present in the roles.<agent>.allowed_tools list of app/policies.yaml — e.g., scout_agent invoking save_intelligence_report or analyst_agent invoking post_slack_notification.
pending_binding_information: That a non-None dict returned from an ADK before_tool_callback actually prevents tool execution is a framework semantic; supplied source shows only the declared contract (docstring at app/safety.py:117-119) and the blocking returns, not the ADK runtime enforcement code.

How ADK populates tool_context.agent_name during sub-agent delegation (app/safety.py:120) is framework-internal and not shown in supplied source, so the agent identity used for allowlist matching is bound only by declaration.
contracts.protected_operation: Agent-initiated tool invocation dispatch for all tools registered on the four agents: fetch_web_page (scout_agent), get_own_pricing_catalog / get_competitor_history / search_competitor_pricing_news (analyst_agent), query_pricing_db / generate_history_chart (db_analyst_agent), and save_intelligence_report / export_pricing_strategy / post_slack_notification (coordinator_agent).
contracts.protected_resource: The agents' tool-execution surface (the Python-function tools registered on the ADK Agent instances and the downstream effects they would perform).
contracts.protection_obligation: Every tool invocation by any ADK agent in this unit (scout_agent, analyst_agent, db_analyst_agent, coordinator_agent) must pass the registered before_tool_callback domain_safety_guard (PolicyService.validate_tool_call) before the tool executes, and the guard must deny any agent/tool pair whose tool name is not listed in that agent's role allowlist in app/policies.yaml. (Merged wording of both reviewers: unauthorized agent-to-tool pairs are blocked at the tool-execution dispatch point, prior to any downstream effect of the tool such as the HTTP page fetch, the Slack webhook POST, or local file/SQLite writes.)
scope_limits: Covers only the before_tool_callback role-gating mechanism; the separate FunctionTool require_confirmation=True flag on export_pricing_strategy (app/agent.py:148-151) is a distinct mechanism not asserted by the reviewed obligations.
transfer_to_agent is unconditionally allowed for every agent (app/safety.py:52-54) and is outside this denial obligation.

This dispatch-point gate transitively guards downstream effects of differing strata (HTTP page fetch, Slack webhook POST at app/tools.py:221-233, file/SQLite writes at app/tools.py:37-151) only insofar as it denies unauthorized agent/tool pairs; it does not perform safety content checks on those tools' arguments (only bracketed-placeholder sanitization at app/safety.py:129-132).
Applicability to tool invocations occurring outside the four registered Agent instances is not established by the supplied source.
